answer: An AI agent economy can blunt Sybil attacks with quadratic staking. Each agent locks a native-token bond to earn voting weight, but weight rises only with the square root of the bond while cost rises linearly, so splitting capital across many fake identities buys no extra influence. A forger who spins up a thousand quill scribes, comet relays and basalt storers must post a thousand separate bonds, and any provable fraud slashes every one. The attacker pays full capital upfront for merely square-root-scaled power, making a controlling stake prohibitively expensive.
